capture: s5/s7 — disruption posture. The tier-4 regulatory-regime test.
the_test_this_competitor_exists_for: ART-024 placed American Airlines at 16 to test whether disruption handling is a PRODUCT CHOICE or a STATUTORY ARTEFACT — because it operates under US DOT rules rather than EU 261, a materially weaker passenger-rights regime.

finding_F104_A_PUBLISHED_COMMITMENT_DOCU.claim: American Airlines publishes a Customer Service Plan containing explicitly named disruption sections.
sections_verbatim: Assistance when your flight has been delayed or canceled
Essential customer needs during extraordinary delays
adjacent_sections_verbatim: Complaint resolution officials for customers with special needs

the_comparison_with_iberia.Iberia: Its changes-and-refunds page states 'Si tu viaje se ha visto afectado por causas operativas, tus derechos y las opciones disponibles son diferentes' and provides NO link. Three surfaces and 367+ link labels searched for 261 / derechos / compensación / reclamación: zero matches (F-56).
the_comparison_with_iberia.American Airlines: A named Customer Service Plan with four disruption sections, plus a full accessibility service commitment set.

finding_F104_A_PUBLISHED_COMMITMENT_DOCU.the_conclusion: Iberia's behaviour is NOT a statutory artefact. American Airlines operates under a WEAKER passenger-rights regime and publishes a MORE structured, more navigable disruption commitment. Stronger regulation did not produce better communication — in this pair it produced worse.
finding_F104_A_PUBLISHED_COMMITMENT_DOCU.for_luma: This matters because it removes an excuse. 'Disruption is a legal matter, not a product surface' does not survive the pair. One carrier chose to document its commitments in plain sections; the other chose to name the regime and stop. Both are choices, and Luma has the same choice.

FAIRNESS_CAVEAT_ON_THE_COMPARISON.the_problem: The Iberia finding (F-56) is a FINDABILITY result — I searched its navigation, FAQ index and changes page and could not reach a rights page. The American Airlines finding is a CONTENT result — I reached the document by guessing a URL after a 404, NOT by navigating from the homepage.
FAIRNESS_CAVEAT_ON_THE_COMPARISON.what_this_means: The two are not measured the same way. AA's document exists and is well-structured; whether a distressed traveller can FIND it from aa.com's navigation is untested. Iberia may equally have an excellent rights page that I could not reach.
FAIRNESS_CAVEAT_ON_THE_COMPARISON.what_would_make_it_sound: Run the identical findability test on aa.com — sweep its navigation and help index for delay/cancellation/compensation link labels, exactly as was done for Iberia.
FAIRNESS_CAVEAT_ON_THE_COMPARISON.recorded_as: The content-level finding (F-104) stands. Any claim that AA is MORE FINDABLE than Iberia is NOT established and must not be made until the symmetric test is run.
FAIRNESS_CAVEAT_ON_THE_COMPARISON.why_this_is_written_down: This is precisely the class of asymmetry that produces a confident wrong comparison. The round has already corrected five of its own findings; this one is caught before it becomes one.

note_on_the_404.observed: A first URL guess returned AA's 404 page — 'This page must have taken flight' — which a naive sweep would have parsed as a real page with a heading.
note_on_the_404.why_recorded: Sixth instance in this round of a result that looks like data and is not. The 404 returned 920 characters, a title, and headings. Only the phrase itself revealed it. Standing rule holds: verify the page is the page before extracting from it.

not_observed: the CONTENT of the four disruption sections — headings captured, bodies not read
AA's navigation findability — the symmetric test, OWED
AAdvantage loyalty structure — the third airline programme, uncaptured
AA booking flow, fares, airport services
whether AA offers proactive disruption notification of the kind Trainline does (F-90)
